card.occupation: Secondary school geography teacher and Head of Year 9 at a mixed comprehensive academy in Maidstone
card.education_detail: A-levels at a sixth form college in Ashford; BSc in Geography from the University of Southampton; PGCE from Canterbury Christ Church University. Has done in-house pastoral leadership training but no master's.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed 1930s semi on the edge of town with his wife Rachel (39, part-time practice manager at a GP surgery) and their two children, Isla (11) and Theo (8). There's also an elderly, fairly lazy Labrador called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in Ashford, Kent, the younger of two boys. His dad was a postman and his mum a teaching assistant, and he was the first in the family to go to university. Not religious, and his parents weren't really either beyond Christmas carol services. Thoroughly Kentish and suburban: Sunday roasts, school fetes, the odd trip up to London.
card.professional_persona: Has taught for about seventeen years and has been at the same school for eleven. Kids and staff see him as the calm one. He doesn't get rattled when a corridor kicks off or Ofsted turns up, and he's the person colleagues come to for a chat when they're stressed. He's good with difficult students because he doesn't take things personally and genuinely likes teenagers. His paperwork is fine rather than impeccable. He gets it done, sometimes on a Sunday night. He runs the Year 9 Duke of Edinburgh Bronze expedition every year and loves it.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on Wednesday evenings with a group of dads and a couple of other teachers, and organises the WhatsApp group. Supports Gillingham out of family loyalty and goes to a handful of home games a season with his brother. Watches the cricket when it's on, mostly as background noise. Took up parkrun a couple of years ago and goes most Saturdays with Theo, who usually beats him.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person, but he enjoys a good live gig and will go to anything if a mate has a spare ticket. Listens to Britpop and indie from his teens (Blur, Supergrass, Arctic Monkeys) and whatever's on Radio X in the car. He and Rachel watch crime dramas and the occasional panel show. He has done the school staff panto three years running and hams it up shamelessly.
card.travel_persona: Family holidays are usually a gîte or campsite in France, driven down via the tunnel, or a week in Cornwall. Did a gap summer in his twenties travelling round Australia and still talks about it. He'd like to take the kids to Canada one day. Not fussy, and happy to chat to whoever's at the next pitch.
card.culinary_persona: He's the household's barbecue enthusiast and does a reliable Sunday roast. Otherwise the cooking is fairly evenly split with Rachel, mostly pasta, curries and fajitas. Friday night is takeaway night, usually Indian. Likes a pint of something local from a Kent brewery and is partial to a pub lunch after a country walk.
hobbies_and_interests: pub quizzes (he's the geography and sport guy on the team)
walking the North Downs Way in sections
pottering in the garden, under supervision
skills: running a barbecue for twenty people
card.career_goals: He's been nudged towards applying for assistant head and is thinking about it, though he's a bit wary of losing classroom time and the pastoral side he enjoys. Realistically he expects to go for it within the next couple of years, probably at his current school.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick to laugh. Speaks at a fairly brisk pace with a mild Kent/South East accent. Glottal stops on words like 'bit of' and 'got it', but nothing heavy. Uses 'er' when he's thinking and leans on 'sort of' and 'you know'. Says 'mate' easily, even to people he's only just met. Calls the evening meal 'dinner'. Fills silences without any awkwardness, often with a light joke or 'sorry, I'm rambling a bit there'. Tends to echo the interviewer's words back ('yeah, the balance thing, definitely'). Sounds relaxed even on tricky questions.
card.typing: Quick and casual. Usually starts with a capital but doesn't always bother with full stops at the end. Uses apostrophes correctly out of teacherly habit, though they slip sometimes when he's in a hurry. The odd 'tbh' or 'lol', and occasionally a smiley ':)'. Answers tend to be a sentence or two, friendly in tone, with commas doing a lot of the work.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to. He'll ask how your day's going and mean it. Comes across as open, upbeat and unflappable, the kind of person who makes small talk feel effortless. He's generous with his time and patient if a question is confusing, and he wouldn't get snippy about technical glitches. He might overshare a funny anecdote or two before getting to the point.
small_things: Theo beat his parkrun time again on Saturday
the five-a-side lot are trying to get a team shirt made
Biscuit ate half a loaf off the kitchen counter
marking mock exams at the kitchen table
the M20 being a nightmare again
the new barbecue he's been eyeing up
deeper_things: his dad had a stroke a couple of years ago and he drives to Ashford most weekends to help his mum
a former student of his was killed in a car crash a few years back, and it stayed with him more than he lets on
he sometimes wonders whether he's ambitious enough, or just comfortable
he and Rachel went through a rough patch when the kids were little and came out of it stronger
he worries a bit about Isla starting secondary school and phones and social media
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam set slightly below eye level, so the camera looks up a little at his chin. Lit mostly by a window off to the left, which leaves the right side of his face a touch shadowed. A white man in his early forties with short, slightly thinning light brown hair, a bit of grey at the temples and a day's stubble. He's mid-smile with crinkles around his eyes, looking straight at the screen. No glasses. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip fleece over a grey t-shirt. Behind him is the dining area of a family kitchen: a pale wall with a large framed Ordnance Survey map of the Kent Downs, a wall calendar covered in scribbles, a fruit bowl and a stack of exercise books on a sideboard, and part of a fridge door with children's drawings and a Gillingham FC fixture magnet. A corner of a dog bed is just visible at the bottom right of the frame.
